ai.title: Refactor template placeholders to enum
ai.summary: Backend template injection logic now uses a PLACEHOLDER enum instead of string arrays for prompt variable management. This replaces manual brace-wrapped string keys in `claude4base.ts` and `strings.ts` with typed enum values, simplifying the `formatPrompt` function and reducing potential typos. The change is internal to the `backend/src/templates` directory and affects how agent prompts are constructed before execution.

eli5.text: You don't see anything change directly. Behind the scenes, the system now uses a fixed list of named options instead of handwritten text labels when filling in parts of the assistant's instructions (things like the tools it can use or a summary of the project's files). This just makes that process less error-prone for the people maintaining it, and doesn't alter what you get back.

ai.title: Add experimental agent template
ai.summary: New `experimental` agent template added to `agentTemplates` in `backend/src/templates/agent-list.ts`, backed by `backend/src/templates/agents/experimental.ts`. This template uses `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05` and is registered in `AgentTemplateNameSchema` in `common/src/types/agent-state.ts`. Existing `claude4base` template moved to `backend/src/templates/agents/claude4base.ts` to support subdirectory organization. No migration needed for existing templates; new template available immediately for selection.

eli5.text: A new option for the assistant's brain, called 'experimental,' is now available to choose from, and it runs on Google's latest Gemini 2.5 Pro model designed for tougher reasoning tasks. If you opened the list of available brains, you'd see this new one alongside the existing default; picking it switches the assistant to that newer model. This is live today, so anyone who can select an assistant brain can now try the experimental one.

ai.title: PLACEHOLDER renamed to strongly typed const
ai.summary: PLACEHOLDER enum replaced with strongly typed const object in backend/src/templates/types.ts. Keys renamed (e.g. TOOLS to TOOLS_PROMPT) to match string values. formatPrompt in strings.ts updated to use PlaceholderValue type and placeholderValues array. Agent templates in claude4base.ts and experimental.ts updated to use new keys.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal instructions were quietly reorganized: the labels that mark where each piece of information (like the list of available tools, the project folder, or system details) gets filled in were given clearer, more descriptive names, and the code that swaps those labels into the prompts now uses a stricter, safer system to catch mistakes. If you looked at how the assistant builds its responses, you'd see it references these clearly named spots instead of short cryptic tags, and the behind-the-scenes logic that assembles prompts is now more rigid about only allowing recognized labels. This is live today for anyone using the assistant's standard or experimental setup.

ai.title: Disallow research tool in readOnlyMode
ai.summary: Updated `getFilteredToolsInstructions` in `backend/src/tools.ts` to accept `readOnlyMode` and exclude `research` and `create_plan` tools when active. Modified `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to pass `readOnlyMode` to the instruction generator and switch `create_plan` gating from `isAskMode` to `readOnlyMode`. This ensures read-only agents cannot initiate research or create plans.

eli5.text: When an agent runs in read-only mode, it can no longer call the research tool or create plans; only write and terminal tools remain restricted by that mode too. Anyone relying on a read-only agent for safe investigation will find those two extra tools silently unavailable, since the filtering step now removes them whenever that mode is on. The behavior is already live today.

ai.title: Add lite and max agent templates
ai.summary: New `lite` and `max` agent templates added to `backend/src/templates/agents/`. `lite` uses `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20` for speed; `max` uses `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` for quality. Both share the updated 'Buffy' system prompt with subgoal tracking and file versioning logic. Registered in `agent-list.ts` and typed in `common/src/types/agent-state.ts`.

eli5.text: When you start a new conversation with the coding assistant, you can now choose between two pre-configured versions of Buffy instead of only one. One version, called 'Lite', uses a faster model so you get answers more quickly, and the other, called 'Max', uses a higher-quality model so you get more accurate answers. Both versions share the same updated instructions that let Buffy track which task she's working on and keep correct records when she edits your files, and this choice is available today when you create a new session.

ai.title: Fix readOnlyMode parameter passing in system prompt
ai.summary: readOnlyMode parameter added to getAgentSystemPrompt call in backend/src/main-prompt.ts. getAgentSystemPrompt signature updated in backend/src/system-prompt/agent-system-prompt.ts to accept and forward readOnlyMode to getFilteredToolsInstructions. getFilteredToolsInstructions in backend/src/tools.ts sets readOnlyMode default to false. Ensures read-only agent mode correctly filters tool instructions.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs in read-only mode (for example, when you're exploring code without making changes), a setting that was previously ignored is now actually passed through to the part of the system that decides which tools are available. The result: read-only mode now correctly hides the tools it should hide instead of pretending to be read-only while still letting those tools through.

ai.title: Rename PLACEHOLDER keys in backend agent templates
ai.summary: PLACEHOLDER.REMAINING_STEPS_PROMPT and PLACEHOLDER.PROJECT_ROOT_PROMPT renamed to PLACEHOLDER.REMAINING_STEPS and PLACEHOLDER.PROJECT_ROOT. PLACEHOLDER.TOOLS, FILE_TREE, SYSTEM_INFO, and GIT_CHANGES renamed to their _PROMPT suffixed counterparts. Updates applied across claude4base, experimental, lite, and max agent templates, plus strings.ts and types.ts.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes labels the system uses to insert live information into an AI assistant's instructions have been renamed for consistency. The change is purely internal housekeeping with no visible effect on how the assistant behaves or responds today. Engineers working on the backend templates and shared configuration files will encounter the updated names when reading or modifying those files, but regular users will notice nothing different.

ai.title: Rename agent templates to model-specific names
ai.summary: Agent template identifiers renamed from generic labels (lite, max, experimental) to model-specific names (gemini25flash_base, gemini25pro_thinking, gemini25pro_base, claude4_base). Backend template files and common type definitions updated to reflect new naming convention. Scope covers backend/src/templates and common/src/types/agent-state.ts. New AgentTemplateNames constant exported for type-safe references.

eli5.text: The system renamed its preset assistant configurations from generic labels like "lite", "max", and "experimental" to names that now match the specific artificial intelligence model behind each one, such as "gemini25flash_base" and "claude4_base". If you looked at the configuration panel today, you would see the new, more descriptive names instead of the old short labels, and the system now uses a single shared list of those names to keep everything consistent. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup of how the system organizes its assistant types, so there is no change to what the assistants can actually do, just how they are labeled internally.

ai.title: Migrate tool format to CodebuffToolCall schema
ai.summary: Refactored internal tool call representation from `ToolCall` to `CodebuffToolCall` across backend and common types. Field names standardized to `toolName`, `toolCallId`, and `args` to align with AI SDK `ToolCallPart` structure. Updated `parseRawToolCall`, `loopMainPrompt`, and XML parsers to handle new schema; `ToolCallError` now includes `toolCallId`. Scope includes `backend/src/tools.ts`, `main-prompt.ts`, and `common/src/actions.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal way of talking about tools it can use has been redesigned. Instead of calling a tool by one name and its settings by another, every tool now uses a consistent format with a clear tool name, a unique id, and a single 'args' block for inputs. This change touches how the assistant plans its next action and how it reads back the results, so behind the scenes the flow is more uniform, though you wouldn't see any difference in how it behaves today.

ai.title: tools.test.ts research mode assertions
ai.summary: Updated `getFilteredToolsInstructions` tests in `backend/src/__tests__/tools.test.ts`. Corrected `ask` mode test to pass `false` for `readOnlyMode`. Added test verifying `research` tool exclusion when `readOnlyMode` is `true`.

eli5.text: You can now turn off research mode whenever you're browsing safely, and the system will stop offering research tools until it's turned back on. The assistant will still let you ask questions normally, but it won't try to dig deeper into answers unless explicitly allowed. This is already active if you're using the ask feature.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.331
ai.summary: Version bumped from 1.0.330 to 1.0.331 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: A new version of the software (1.0.331) has been released, bundling in several smaller changes made over the past couple of days. If you update, you may notice the assistant now uses clearer labels for different AI models when choosing how to respond, and administrators have a new internal area to manage settings and see billing details. Some behind-the-scenes changes were also made to keep things running smoothly, like adjusting how the software reads project folders and removing outdated settings. Most of these changes are already active for users today.

ai.title: Suppress PostHog console errors in analytics
ai.summary: Added `suppressPostHogConsoleErrors` to wrap `console.error` and `console.warn`, filtering messages containing 'posthog' with `PostHogError` name. Modified `flushAnalytics` and `logError` to silently catch PostHog exceptions without logging to console or logger. This prevents internal analytics connection failures from cluttering the user's terminal output. Changes applied in `npm-app/src/utils/analytics.ts`.

eli5.text: You won't see error messages from PostHog cluttering your console anymore. PostHog is the tool that tracks how people use the app, and previously, if it had connection problems or failed to send data, it would print technical error messages to your screen. The system now catches those failures silently behind the scenes, so your terminal stays clean. This affects anyone using the app, especially in internal or development environments.

ai.title: Bump npm package version to 1.0.332
ai.summary: Version bump in `npm-app/package.json` from 1.0.331 to 1.0.332. Covers the `codebuff` npm package manifest. No functional code changes included in this commit.

eli5.text: You don't see anything new when you open the assistant today. This update simply stamps the release number higher in the package that installs the assistant app, so anyone downloading it now gets the version that already quietly hid a stream of analytics error messages from the screen. That error-suppression fix is the only user-visible thing in this batch, and it is now included live for anyone who installs the latest version. Everything else in the snapshot so far (the enum refactor, new agent templates, the read-only mode tweak) is not part of what you experience from this specific version bump.
